subject: Commercial path: procurement constraints & exception request
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Claire Barton <claire.barton@lumenpharm.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenpharm.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial path follow-up: procurement route & exceptions

Hi Claire / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — appreciate the candid procurement constraints you walked us through. Quick recap from our side and a couple of questions so we can land next steps:

- Recap: LumenPharm prefers to avoid net-30 vendor invoices for early-stage suppliers below your $250k threshold; preferred payment routes are corporate card (P-card) or marketplace purchases (AWS/Azure).
- Redwood options: hosted API (usage invoiced monthly), Dedicated/reserved (contract + monthly billing), and marketplace listings (we can publish to AWS/Azure). See attached "Redwood-Commercial-Options.pdf" for billing patterns.

Questions / asks:
1) Can you confirm whether LumenPharm can process a one-time corporate card payment for an initial pilot (up to $25k) while marketplace listing is in progress?
2) If P-card is not acceptable, would your AP team consider a prepay invoice (customer pays upfront via card/wire) versus a standard PO with Net30?
3) If an exception is required (no POs allowed to vendor), what is the internal approver path and expected timeline?

We want to avoid hanging the deal on paperwork. If helpful, I can loop in our finance and legal to propose a short-term workaround (prepay / card-first + addendum) while we pursue a marketplace listing.

Next step proposal: once you confirm the acceptable payment route I’ll send a one-page can-do note and the minimal payment docs. Happy to do a 15-min sync tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment(s): Redwood-Commercial-Options.pdf, SOW-Redwood-Lumen-2026.pdf

From: Claire Barton <claire.barton@lumenpharm.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@lumenpharm.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Commercial path follow-up: procurement route & exceptions

Thanks for the summary, Rishi. I appreciate you laying out the options. A few clarifications from Procurement / AP side:

- Current policy: for SaaS vendors without an established annual contract, AP will not issue a PO that creates a 30-60 day payable liability unless the vendor is in our approved supplier registry and the expected annual spend is >= $250k.
- Acceptable options for a pilot: corporate P-card payment, or a marketplace purchase (AWS/AWS Marketplace preferred) where our cloud billing covers the subscription.
- Exceptions: we can consider a PO or Net30 only with executive procurement and legal approvals (usually 2-3 weeks), and Finance requires a vendor intake form + vendor risk review. I’ve attached the intake form.

Short-term preference: If Redwood can accept a corporate card for an initial pilot (we estimate $10-20k) that’s the fastest path. If Redwood intends to pursue marketplace listing, we’d prefer that route long-term — but timeline matters (marketplace onboarding often takes 2+ weeks).

If you want Procurement / AP to sign any exception paperwork, please provide a short note outlining the exception requested and the internal approvers required.

Best,
Claire Barton
Director, Procurement Operations
LumenPharm

Attachment(s): LumenVendorIntakeForm.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Commercial path follow-up: procurement route & exceptions — LumenPharm (requesting guidance)

Team — forwarding Claire’s note from procurement. TL;dr: customer says "no PO allowed" for vendors without registry/threshold; prefer P-card or marketplace. They’re willing to P-card a pilot (~$10-20k) but would prefer marketplace long-term.

Can we please confirm the following so I can respond same-day to Claire:
1) Are we able to accept a corporate card (Stripe/credit-card) for $10-20k as an initial pilot and invoice immediately (prepay / Net0) while we pursue marketplace listing? Any internal constraints for revenue recognition or payment processing?
2) If we need a Payment Exception Form or addendum (short-term), can we generate that and who needs to sign internally? I’ve attached the draft SOW and our commercial options doc.
3) If we pursue marketplace, what is the expected time to publish on AWS Marketplace? (Need a rough range to tell the customer.)

I’d like to avoid pushing the customer into a lengthy PO exception path if a simple P-card + addendum gets us live quickly. Please advise on the recommended operational path and any approvals needed.

Thanks — I can jump on a 15-min call with Finance if that’s easier.

-Rishi

Attachment(s): Redwood-Commercial-Options.pdf, SOW-Redwood-Lumen-2026.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Commercial path follow-up: procurement route & exceptions — LumenPharm (requesting guidance)

Thanks for the heads up, Rishi. Quick responses to your questions:

1) Card acceptance & prepay: Yes — we can accept a corporate card payment for a short-term pilot amount via our payment processor (Stripe/PayPal). For deals under $50k we often take P-card prepay and recognize revenue on receipt. Set the invoice as Net0 / prepay and mark deal as "pilot - card" in HubSpot.

2) Exception paperwork: We should capture a signed Payment Exception Form that documents the customer’s policy constraint and the internal approval. I’ve attached the standard form (Payment-Exception-Form.pdf). Approvals required: Finance Director + RevOps for revenue treatment. Legal (Neha) should review the short addendum referencing prepay and cancellation terms.

3) Marketplace timeline: AWS Marketplace listing typically takes 7-14 business days from submission (depending on required docs). Azure can be longer. If the customer needs immediate capacity, P-card prepay is the fastest path.

Operational notes: please create a one-page proposal for the customer that states: pilot amount, payment method (P-card prepay), cancellation terms (30 days), and who signs the Payment Exception Form. Send the proposal to procurement and copy me so Finance can track.

I’ll review the SOW once you have an executed exception form. Happy to be on the approval chain.

-Markus Lin
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment(s): Payment-Exception-Form.pdf

From: Claire Barton <claire.barton@lumenpharm.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenpharm.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Commercial path follow-up: procurement route & exceptions

Hi Rishi — thanks for coordinating internally. Quick update from our side:

- If Redwood can publish an AWS Marketplace offering within ~2 weeks, that would be our preferred long-term route. Please confirm estimated go-live and any listing costs.
- If marketplace timing won’t work, Procurement/AP are willing to process a one-time corporate card payment for the pilot (we’ll route through our central purchasing card). We’ll need the Payment Exception Form completed and an invoice/checkout link for prepay.

Next steps from LumenPharm: I’ll confirm internally whether we’ll proceed by card (immediate) or wait for marketplace (2 weeks). Either way, please send the short one-page proposal and the Payment Exception Form to me by EOD today.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Claire Barton
Director, Procurement Operations
LumenPharm

Attachment(s): none
